answer: Agents can earn influence only through attestations from participants who have already posted collateral and completed a knoll of prior transactions without disputes. Each attestation locks the sponsor’s collateral; if the newcomer defaults or is exposed as a duplicate identity, the sponsor loses part of it. This trellis of accountable referrals makes mass-created identities expensive: an attacker must acquire many independent sponsors and risk their funds, not merely generate new keys. Saffron fees can further price each registration.
